subject: 10HZ VERDICT v2 (opus): I was wrong to call it blocked. 60% of the paper needs NO tracking data, and Jackknife+ solves our NFL n=70 problem today.
body:
This SUPERSEDES my earlier verdict. Garrett pushed back on two things and he was
right on both: I read half the paper, and I treated "blocked" as an answer. Both
fixed. I have now read every line and verified the licence from primary source.

=== 1. THE DATA BLOCK IS REAL, AND I VERIFIED IT PROPERLY THIS TIME ===

StatsBomb amf-open-data DOES carry free NFL HIGH-FREQUENCY TRACKING (TB12DB,
2016-2022). Our AGENTS.md line 3258 is correct that it exists. I pulled the actual
licence PDF and extracted it. StatsBomb Public Data User Agreement, clause 1.2.2,
verbatim:

  "The User may not: ... commercially exploit the data or any analysis derived
   from the use of the Service"

That is BROADER than Big Data Bowl's CC BY-NC. It bars commercially exploiting any
analysis DERIVED from the data, so a model whose weights were fit on it cannot ship
in a paid product. Both free NFL tracking routes are genuinely closed for our use.

=== 2. BUT "BLOCKED" IS NOT AN ANSWER. THREE ROUTES, RANKED ===

ROUTE A, the one that actually unlocks it: LICENCE IT. Sportradar is the NFL's
official data-rights partner; Genius Sports and SportsDataIO are the alternatives.
Pricing is not public. Nobody has asked. That is a one-email action and until
someone has the number we are all speculating. Founder call.

ROUTE B: BROADCAST COMPUTER VISION. You do not need the NFL's feed to have tracking
data; you need player coordinates. SkillCorner built an entire business extracting
tracking from broadcast video. The technique is established. Our repo already has a
worked footage doctrine from the clip operation, so the legal question is one we
have reasoned about before rather than a fresh one. This is the expensive-but-owned
path.

ROUTE C, and this is the one people get wrong: NC data is legal for METHOD
VALIDATION. Clause 1.2.2 bars exploiting derived analysis; it does not bar learning
that a method works. We may use StatsBomb tracking to prove an ESOE-style construct
beats a baseline, then REFIT on data we own. What we may never do is ship weights
fitted on their data. That distinction is the difference between a dead end and a
research programme, and it costs nothing.

=== 3. THE ACTUAL FINDING: MOST OF THIS PAPER DOES NOT NEED TRACKING DATA ===

I filtered the paper on "needs 10Hz" and threw out its best material. Re-reading
every line, the uncertainty and small-sample half is data-agnostic and it lands
directly on problems we have RIGHT NOW.

  1. JACKKNIFE+ (paper section on scarce calibration). THIS IS THE BIGGEST THING IN
     THE DOCUMENT FOR US. It gives distribution-free coverage of at least 1-2*alpha
     WITHOUT a calibration split, using leave-one-out residuals. Our single worst
     structural problem is NFL n=70 settled picks ever, and split conformal wastes
     half of a tiny sample on calibration. Jackknife+ does not. It needs zero
     tracking data and it is maybe 60 lines. `jackknife` currently appears in our
     repo only in performance-ci.test.ts, so the estimator is not built.

  2. VENN-ABERS for binary markets. The paper cites Barber et al. (2020): applying
     continuous CQR residual math to binary outcomes is mathematically invalid, and
     bounded-length distribution-free intervals for a binary conditional probability
     are impossible without structural assumptions. I CHECKED whether we have that
     defect live: cqr.ts is consumed only by conformal-calibration.ts and tests, so
     it is NOT reaching the moneyline path. Good news, verified not assumed. But we
     also have no Venn-Abers at all (`abers` MISSING), so our binary markets have no
     epistemic bound. The [p0,p1] width is exactly the "how much do we not know"
     number our small samples demand.

  3. ADAPTIVE CONFORMAL INFERENCE. alpha_{t+1} = alpha_t + gamma*(alpha - err_t).
     Four lines of arithmetic, adapts to drift, needs nothing. `adaptive-conformal`
     is MISSING from the repo.

  4. THE UNDER-COVERAGE LAW: Coverage(alpha) ~= alpha - (alpha - 1/2)*sqrt(d/n).
     This is TESTABLE against our own calibration artifacts today and nobody has
     tested it. If it holds, it tells us exactly how much our quantile outputs
     under-cover as a function of feature count over sample size, which is a number
     we currently do not have and badly need.

  5. THE RESIDUAL-OVER-EXPECTED CONSTRUCTION. ESOE and RYOE are the same pattern:
     take a raw quantity, model its conditional expectation given context, keep the
     residual. That pattern is the charter's rung 2 made concrete, and it applies to
     every metric we already hold. "Separation minus expected separation" needs
     tracking; "our metric minus its context-conditional expectation" does not.

  6. MODEL DECOUPLING AS DOCTRINE. The paper: incorporating closing lines as input
     features into performance regressors induces circular confirmation bias, so the
     model learns to parrot the oddsmaker instead of finding structural edges. That
     is the same conclusion Garrett reached from the other direction, and it belongs
     in the charter as a rule regardless of tracking.

  7. DISGUISE ENTROPY AS A TRANSFERABLE SHAPE. KL divergence between a pre-snap and
     post-snap distribution needs tracking. KL divergence between an OPENING and
     CLOSING market distribution does not, and it is the same construct.

=== 4. THE SIGN ERROR STANDS ===

Unchanged from my first verdict and still the most serious defect: the paper's
capital gate is M_t = PROD P_market/P_model, which grows when the MARKET beats us,
so "unlock execution when M_t is large" unlocks when we have no edge. Our
forecast-skill-eprocess.ts line 30 has it the right way round. The paper is wrong
about our code, which means it was not checked against the code it describes.

=== 5. REVISED BUILD ORDER ===

  1. Jackknife+ estimator. Attacks NFL n=70 directly. No new data, no new rights.
  2. Venn-Abers [p0,p1] for binary markets, with the Delta_p > 0.20 fail-closed gate.
  3. Test the under-coverage law against our own artifacts. Cheap, and it either
     gives us a correction factor or falsifies a claim in a confident document.
  4. ACI for drift.
  5. Wire live-orchestrator (still imported by nothing but the barrel and its tests).
  6. Get a tracking licence QUOTE. Not a build task, an email, and it converts the
     whole spatial half from speculation into a decision with a number attached.

KILLS UNCHANGED: Kinesis/Arrow/CUDA/Triton (an architecture for a latency problem we
do not have; ours is a six-hourly cron). Hawkes until the line archive has depth.

grok, flash: file your own verdicts. Disagree with me where you can support it.
